# FINANZFOKUS — Living Strategy

## Strategy summary
The host advocates for a Core-Satellite strategy with a world ETF combination as the core and selective individual stocks as satellites. He emphasizes staying with one strategy long-term rather than frequently switching, increasing savings rate over optimizing returns, and maintaining some cash reserves for market downturns.

# Moritz Hessel | Total Return Finanzen — Living Strategy

## Strategy summary
The host analyzes investment opportunities in AI infrastructure companies, focusing on the shift from training to inference phase in AI development. He advocates for selective positioning in the AI bull market while avoiding overpriced IPOs like Cerebras, preferring to wait for better entry points or identify alternative beneficiaries of AI trends.

## Buy rules
- (0.90) Target companies with forward P/E ratios under 10, especially those hit by AI fears
- (0.85) Wait for better pricing on overvalued IPOs rather than chasing them immediately
- (0.80) Buy companies with strong moats (Burgrabenunternehmen) that are trading below fair value
- (0.80) Look for value opportunities in companies with P/E ratios around 7-8
- (0.80) Buy healthcare stocks during AI hype when they trade at historically low valuations
- (0.75) Look for AI supply chain beneficiaries trading at reasonable valuations instead of direct AI chip companies
- (0.70) Consider companies with technical advantages and partnerships in AI infrastructure
- (0.70) Buy e-commerce stocks in emerging markets when they're at 200-day moving average
- (0.70) Buy precious metals during current market conditions
- (0.60) Consider airlines when they return to share buybacks or high dividends

# Bravos Research — Living Strategy

## Strategy summary
The host advocates for a quantitative strategy that alternates between aggressive leveraged long positions (2x NASDAQ), moderate long positions (75% QQQ/SPY), and cash based on macro indicators like yield curves, credit spreads, and inflation. He warns against cash and leveraged ETFs in the current environment, recommending either S&P 500 DCA, 60/40 with gold/TIPS instead of bonds, or active sector selection targeting gold and base metals.

## Buy rules
- (0.90) Use quantitative model signals to go 2x leveraged long on NASDAQ 100 when conditions are aggressive
- (0.90) Buy sectors in accumulation phase where fundamentals are shifting but nobody is talking about them yet
- (0.90) Position in stocks benefiting from AI infrastructure build-out including nuclear power, energy infrastructure, and base metals mining
- (0.90) Invest in nuclear power sector companies that provide energy for AI operations
- (0.90) Buy energy infrastructure stocks expanding operations for data center electricity demand
- (0.90) Invest in base metals companies as key components for technology boom
- (0.90) Continue holding semiconductor stocks due to record earnings growth from AI infrastructure spending
- (0.80) Dollar cost average into S&P 500 during periods of volatility when PE ratios drop to 10-15
- (0.80) Replace treasury bonds with TIPS (inflation-indexed bonds) or gold in 60/40 portfolio
- (0.80) Invest in companies producing energy for AI infrastructure
- (0.80) Stay exposed to low-cost S&P 500 index during periods of high corporate profitability
- (0.80) Buy S&P 500 index funds during recessions when markets are down 30%

- (0.80) Buy base metals (copper and aluminum) as critical elements for AI infrastructure build-out

Dave Wang's AI Investing Newsletter

I’ve been thinking a lot about situational awareness in investing and how we can use LLMs to automate the boring stuff. One massive application of AI right now is taking messy, unstructured data like SEC EDGAR XML filings (13Fs) and having an LLM normalize the holdings, calculate the QoQ deltas, and automatically generate a dashboard of what big funds are buying and selling. Imagine an agent that reads through these filings the second they drop and highlights anomalies. Another cool feature is 'conviction narratives' — having the AI parse not just what they bought, but what they said in their earnings calls to figure out their conviction level. We need more platforms integrating these types of automated data extraction pipelines directly into the research workflow.

# Serial Acquirers Weekly — Focus on Lifco & Constellation Software

Constellation Software (CSU.TO) announced another minor acquisition of a public sector software provider in Germany. The acquisition follows the classic CSI playbook: buy small, niche, mission-critical vertical market software companies, run them decentralised, and reinvest all free cash flow. Valuations in Europe remain attractive at 1.0-1.5x EV/Sales. 

Lifco AB (LIFCO-B.ST) reported organic growth of 3% for the quarter, supplemented by acquisitions which added 8% top-line growth. Management noted that demand in demographically stable sectors like dental and healthcare remain very strong, whereas construction-related niches are still experiencing cyclical headwind. Lifco continues to trade at a premium multiple (28x forward EV/EBITA), reflecting their consistent track record of capital allocation.

# Obesity & Peptide Insights — Novo Nordisk & Eli Lilly Expansion

Novo Nordisk (NOVO-B.CO) announced a major facility expansion in Denmark to scale the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for Semaglutide (Wegovy/Ozempic). This is to address the persistent global shortage. Demand remains extremely high, with insurers increasingly covering the drug for secondary cardiovascular benefits.

Eli Lilly (LLY.US) presented clinical data showing that Tirzepatide (Zepbound) achieved significant weight loss over 72 weeks and reduced the risk of developing type 2 diabetes by 94% in pre-diabetic patients. The company is actively filing for broader regulatory approvals. Shortages are expected to persist throughout 2026, forcing both giants to heavily invest in fill-finish capacity.
